---
title: 6 - Legend
---

You will create a map legend that explains the colours and patterns used for the thematic layers. You will build its content in `index.html` and control its appearance in `style.css`.

A useful legend should explain the map's symbols without hiding too much of the map. In this chapter, we will place a compact legend in the upper-right corner.


## 6.1. Create the legend container

- [ ] Open `index.html`.
- [ ] Find the map container `<div id="map" class="map">`.
- [ ] Add the legend markup **inside the map container**, on the next indentation:

```html
<body>
    <div id="map" class="map">

      <!-- Map legend -->
      <div id="legend">
        Stuff for our legend will be here.
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- JavaScript application -->
    <script type="module" src="main.js"></script>
  </body>
```

```html
<!-- Map legend -->
      <div id="legend">
        Some stuff for our legend.
    </div>
```

- [ ] Save the `index.html` file and preview the changes on your webmap. See the small text in the upper-right corner? That's your legend (for now)!


## 6.2. Position and style the legend

- [ ] Open `style.css` file and add the following rules at the the end of the existing code:

```css
/* ----------------------------------------
    Legend
---------------------------------------- */
#legend {
  position: absolute;
  top: 10px;
  right: 10px;
  z-index: 10;
  background: white;
  opacity: 0.95;
  border-radius: 5px;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25);
  padding: 5px 10px;
}

#legend p {
  margin: 10px 0 5px;
}

.legend-item {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  margin: 5px 0;
}
```

- `#legend { }` defines where the legend container is positioned and how the it looks like - a white box with some shadow and other tweaks. `z-index: 10` makes sure the legend is written on top of the map.

- `#legend p { }` on the other hand defines how normal paragraph text inside the legend will be spaced.

`.legend-item { }` defines placement of the coloured boxes that match with our layers' visualisations.


## 6.3. Add legend symbols and labels

The legend needs a label and a symbol that match each layer on the map. These will be configured with both `index.html` and `style.css` files.

- [ ] Remove the `Stuff for our legend will be here.` placeholder, and make sure the `<div id="legend">` is followed by the code below. Make sure the style categories are once again **inside** the legend item by increasing the indentation one step further.

```html
<!-- Map legend -->
      <div id="legend">

        <!-- Forest reserve layers -->
        <p><strong>Forest reserves</strong></p>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch forest-reserve"></span>
          Forest reserve
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch forest-plantation"></span>
          Forest plantation
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch nature-reserve"></span>
          Nature forest reserve
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch village-reserve"></span>
          Village land forest reserve
        </div>

        <p><strong>National parks and conservation areas</strong></p>

        <!-- Conservation area layers -->
        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch national-park"></span>
          National park
        </div>

        <div class="legend-item">
          <span class="legend-swatch international-area"></span>
          International conservation area
        </div>
      </div>
```
- [ ] Save `index.html` and preview your webmap.


Now, populate the legend with **correct symbol styles**. 

::: {.callout-note}
When creating the legend from scratch with this method, you will add the symbol colours and fill patterns **manually**. If you change the layer fill colors, you need to change them in the legend, too. Other approaches, such as using some popular OpenLayers plugins automates this process.
:::

- [ ] Open `style.css`
- [ ] Copy the following CSS rules and paste them at the end of your `style.css` file:


```css
/* ----------------------------------------
    Legend symbols (match with layer visualisation)
---------------------------------------- */
/* Forest reserve categories */
.forest-reserve {
  background: #006b00;
}

.forest-plantation {
  background: #d3f226;
}

.nature-reserve {
  background: #81bf00;
}

.village-reserve {
  background: #56cf68;
}
/* National parks layer */
.national-park {
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(
    45deg,
    #000000,
    #000000 1px,
    transparent 1px,
    transparent 7px
  );
  border: 1px solid #000000;
}

/* International conservation areas layer */
.international-area {
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(
    135deg,
    #000000,
    #000000 1px,
    transparent 1px,
    transparent 7px
  );
  border: 1px solid #000000;
}
```
- [ ] Double-check that the HEX colour codes match with the actual layer styles in `main.js`
- [ ] Save and view your changes on the webmap. 


**[SCREENSHOT 6.3: Show the finished legend on top of the map. Check that symbols are large enough to distinguish and labels are not clipped.]**


::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint

- The legend is positioned in the upper-right corner.
- Each layer has a label and a symbol (except OpenStreetMap, which is not yet visible in the legend).
- The legend symbols match the styles of the GeoJSON and WMS layers.

If the legend is hidden behind the map, check that it is inside the map container and has a suitable `z-index`.
:::
